title: Treasury Operations Schedule — Payout Methods and Association Check Terms for Member Equities & Patronage
content:
Cash leaving a Member Equities & Patronage holding — cash patronage, retirement or redemption proceeds — is paid by the methods and on the check terms below, class by class.

## Payout terms by class

| | Class C Participation Certificate | Class A Nonvoting Common Stock | Class B Voting Stock | Qualified Allocated Surplus | Nonqualified Allocated Surplus | Class H Preferred Stock |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Payouts may be made by direct deposit | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Cash on the class may be applied to one of the member's loans instead of paid out | No | No | No | Yes | No | No |
| How retirement or redemption proceeds are paid | Check or direct deposit | Check or direct deposit | Check or direct deposit | Check or direct deposit | Check or direct deposit | Check or direct deposit |
| Calendar days after its issue date after which an uncashed association check is void | 180 | 180 | 180 | 180 | 180 | 180 |
| Business days after a check's issue date before a check reported lost may be voided and reissued | 10 | 10 | 10 | 10 | 10 | 10 |
| Years after a payout check goes stale before uncollected funds are reported to the state as unclaimed property | 3 | 3 | 3 | 3 | 3 | 3 |

## Notes

- Applying cash to a loan is available on Qualified Allocated Surplus only, the class on which cash patronage is booked as payable.
- The check terms are the same for every class: a check is void 180 calendar days after its issue date when uncashed; a check reported lost may be voided and reissued once 10 business days have passed since its issue date; funds left uncollected are reported as unclaimed property 3 years after the check goes stale.

**Hypothetical illustration.** An association check issued on 13 March and never cashed is still outstanding on the 180th calendar day after that date; once it is outstanding beyond that day it is void.
